sentences.text: According to the petitioner, he submitted an application for a license to conduct the meat stall for the year 2024-25, and the 1 st respondent issued Ext.P10 denying the same.

Against the denial of license in the application dated 04/04/2024, the petitioner filed Appeal No.276/2024 before the Tribunal for Local Self Government Institutions, and the Tribunal issued Ext.P4 order, and thereafter it was disposed of by Ext.P11 order, since the 1st respondent had rejected the application.

The petitioner submitted Ext.P14 application for license to conduct the meat stall, it was accepted by the 1st respondent as per Ext.P15, and the petitioner remitted Building Tax as per Ext.P16 and submitted Ext.P17 application for license and the 1st respondent rejected the application as per Ext.P18 by contending that the petitioner has not complied with Rule 38 of the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Slaughter Houses and Meat Stalls) Rules, 1996.

sentences.text: According to the petitioner, upon going through Exts. P1 to P4, P6 to P9, and P12 to P17, the petitioner is eligible and entitled to obtain a license to conduct a meat stall on the property.

But, the petitioner contends that the respondents, on 2025:KER:88733 WP(C) NO.41298 OF 2025 a misconception of facts and law, declined the application by Exhibit P18 order on flimsy grounds is the submission.
According to the petitioner, the Ext.P18 order is liable to be set aside and the license is to be issued.

It is the definite case of the petitioner that the petitioner's application is for a license for a private market in accordance with Section 222 of the Kerala Panchayath Raj Act,
1994.
Hence, this Writ Petition.

3. Heard the counsel appearing for the petitioner and the Standing Counsel appearing for the Panchayat.
4.
The short point raised by the petitioner is that the Panchayat proceeded with the application, as if the petitioner was trying to establish a public market.
The definite case of the petitioner is that the petitioner's application is to be considered in the light of Section 222 of the Kerala Panchayath Raj Act, 1994.

The counsel for the petitioner also took me through the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in Peter v. Perayam Panchayat [1996 KHC 77], in which it is stated that the Panchayat have no power or right to auction out the right to conduct private markets.
It will be better to extract the relevant 2025:KER:88733 WP(C) NO.41298 OF 2025 portion of the judgment.
" 5. The question for consideration is whether Exts. P4 and P6 notifications are legally valid.
A conspectus of the provisions of the Act and the relevant rules reveal the following: S.221 of the Act gives power to the Panchayat to provide places to be used as public markets.
Sub-S.2 of S.221 enables the Panchayat to parcel out any portion of a public market and lease such parcel or parcels by auction or otherwise (emphasis supplied).
S.222 deals with licensing of private markets.
Under S.222, no person shall open a new private market or continue to keep open a private market unless he has obtained a licence from the village Panchayat.
No Rules have been framed under the Act regarding public markets and private markets.
As per S.284 of the Act, the rules already in force will continue till new rules are framed.
Under the Kerala Panchayat Act, 1960, Kerala Panchayats (Public and Private Markets) Rules, 1964 were made.

Paragraph No.13 is the relevant portion relied upon by the petitioner and the same is extracted hereunder:
"13.
At this juncture, it may also be relevant to note the existence of the following Rules as well, framed under the relevant sections.
S.R.O.76/96 refers to the Rules framed for licensing Dangerous and Offensive Rules (D & O Rules).
S.R.O. 570/96 pertains to the formalities in respect of Control and Licensing of Public and Private Markets (C & L Rules).
Under the D & O Licence Rules, in respect of the scheduled activities, R.4 provides that licence from the Panchayat is mandatory.
Only prescribed fee is leviable, and licence is valid for one year.
By R.4 of the C & L Rules it is permissible for a licensee of a private market to segregate special area or stall for different commodities.
There is, of course, control for the Panchayat to certain region of the activities of a licensee.

Under R.18(4) in respect of sale of meat, therefore,
licence from the Panchayat also is essential.
In respect of the petitioners, therefore the question is whether the Panchayat has imposed restrictions, over and above those what could have legally been prescribed.

sentences.text: From the discussions aforementioned above, the following principles emerge, as governing the situation.
i) The licensee of the private market is the competent person to grant licence for sale or exposure for sale of any animals or articles in or upon such market.
But, a vendor has also to apply and get a licence under the D & O Rules.

ii) Licensee of a private market may levy fees in any 2025:KER:88733 WP(C)
NO.41298 OF 2025 private market for use of or right to expose goods for sale in such market, and levy fee for other facilities, admissible under S.223 of the Act.
iii) The Panchayat is authorised to insist for only one - third of the gross income of the owner from a private market, when permission is granted to him for levying licence fee.
iv) A Village Panchayath is authorised to levy fee only in respect of a public market in respect of right to expose goods for sale in such market.
v) Only public markets within the Panchayath Area are under the control and management of the Panchayath.
Supervision at limited areas however could be made in respect of private markets.

vi) The Village Panchayath is authorised to parcel out any portion of a public market,
and lease such parcels by auction or otherwise on levy of fee, as stipulated by S.221 of the Act.
This right is not there for them in respect of a stall of private market.

vii) R.38 to 40 of the Slaughter Houses Rules have to be observed by a vendee,
irrespective of whether or not the shop is in a public or private market.

"
6. In the light of the above principles, I am of the considered opinion that the license application of the petitioner is to be reconsidered, and the application is to be considered as if it were an application for the private market in tune with Section 222 of Kerala Panchayath Raj Act, 1994.

Therefore, this Writ Petition (C) is allowed in the following manner:
1. Ext.18 and Ext.R2(a) are set aside.
2. The respondent Panchayat is directed to reconsider the application of the petitioner for the license, treating the application as an application for the license for the private market in accordance with Section 222 of the Kerala Panchayath Raj Act,
1994.
